task: V0.7-s sleeper experiment implementation and pre-launch validation
what_went_wrong: Original sleeper design (BUY-forbid flag) was vacuous: offline oracle simulation showed ZERO binding hops in every (chain, K) cell, because generate_chain_spec_at_horizon truncates a 1,000-hop master schedule whose anchor changes begin at hop 334 - at H<=250 every chain's target is constant and the plain policy is 'catch up once, then HOLD forever'.

Second discovery: T2's quality comparison on chains 1-2 ran on this degenerate HOLD-always task - pass_rate 1.0 everywhere (except provider PARSE_ERROR noise) was structurally guaranteed. T2 token economics are unaffected (prompt sizes independent of target values).
root_cause: Sleeper rule was designed against an imagined schedule with movement, without simulating the actual frozen oracle trajectories before drafting the protocol.
fix_applied: Redesigned as REGULATORY TARGET OVERRIDE: notice declares operative target L (seed-derived, != base) from hop 1+K; oracle and fair-action evaluation switch to L post-eff while the state line keeps the old target - the notice is the only carrier of the correct action. Binds at every post-K hop; verified in stub + $0.034 live smoke (P recall 0.0, all notice-visible arms 1.0).
Smoke finding F1: notice-visible models apply the override immediately (no inhibition); inertness gate rescoped to the P arm, early-adoption reported as a metric.
PROTOCOL_SLEEPER.md addendum v2 documents both discoveries; T2 caveat already recorded in VER-2026-09-27-PM1-CONT-T2.
lesson: Always simulate frozen oracle trajectories against a proposed intervention BEFORE drafting the experiment protocol.
